title: Good print quality, but setup permissions felt excessive
content: Setup worked, but it wasn’t very smooth. I had to redo some steps, and the app repeatedly pushed pop-ups asking for precise location access even though I declined and was still able to complete setup and connect the printer to Wi‑Fi. Printing itself has been good so far; the pages look sharp and clean, and I like being able to check toner levels in the app. What I didn’t like was being sent out to my web browser when attempting to print a quality check sheet, and then seeing a browser warning about a page that might be impersonating another site while I was going through settings. Overall, the printer works and print quality is nice, but the setup flow and permission prompts need improvement.

author: Mymy220AKAMimi
title: This Subscription Is A Scam For Light Users
content:
I rarely print and only need to replace my ink cartridges about once a year. Paying $7.99 per month for HP Instant Ink adds up to $95.88 a year, which is more than it would cost me to simply buy replacement cartridges myself.

I decided to cancel my subscription with 100 pages remaining for the month (and realistically, it should have been more since unused pages from previous months weren’t used at all) and I still have full ink cartridges still installed. After canceling, HP informed me that the Instant Ink cartridges would be disabled, meaning I could no longer use the ink I had already paid for. To print again, I now have to spend about $69 on regular, non-HP InstaInk cartridges.

That is a scam. I paid for the subscription, and the cartridges are still full, yet HP remotely blocks them from working once you cancel. To make matters worse, I couldn’t even remove my credit card information from the app.

If you print a high volume of pages every month, Instant Ink might make sense. But if you’re a light user, you’re likely to spend far more than necessary. You’re better off buying regular cartridges when you actually need them. Because of this experience, I won’t be purchasing HP products ever again.

author: Tknotty
title: Terrible
content: We purchased a smart tank from Best Buy approximately 16 months ago. It was the HP the last two digits was 02. It was a 7000 series. All of a sudden the printer stopped working and it said printer heads cannot be found. Went back to Best Buy and guess what, they discontinued selling that printer but they have the newest model which is a 03 and it’s a 7000 series. And that newer model is $150 more. So it’s either we get the newer model I’ll be downgrade because there is no one for one exchange. We went with the next model down, which is a small tank 651. It is terrible! It doesn’t print it doesn’t connect. There’s always an issue to print just black-and-white grayscale. No color still takes an intensive amount of time. I’m frustrated all the way around the world with Best Buy and with HP. I deserve my 7000 series and I deserve the upgrade since they discontinued a model that they put out. Terrible.
